sampling_model.design: \(n\) independent draws from \(P\), with the covariate law known to be uniform on \([0,1]^d\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in[0,1]^d\times\{0,1\}\times[0,1]^m\) and has potential outcomes \(Y_i(0),Y_i(1)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with consistency and \(Y(1)\perp A\mid X\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensity and treated conditional density are unknown. Smoothness indices and \(L\) are known for tuning. Class membership concerns only primitive laws; no pilot or coefficient estimator is assumed to attain a rate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 transfers any oracle generative lower bound to factual generation, Theorem 3 gives a total-variation upper bound with a first-order nuisance product, and Section 7 states that the oracle lower bound may be loose when nuisances are nonsmooth.

In arXiv:1902.01778v4, Section 2.2.1, Theorem 1 and its display on PDF page 6 give the positive-density expected Wasserstein upper rate over the stated Besov class, and Theorem 3 and its display on the same page give the corresponding all-estimator lower rate; at transport order \(1\) and density dimension \(m\ge3\), the oracle rate exponent is \((s+1)/(2s+m)\).

In arXiv:2102.12034v1, equation (3) on PDF page 4 defines the marginal counterfactual density, equation (6) on page 6 defines its fixed finite-dimensional projection, Theorem 1 with equation (17) on page 13 gives the projection influence function, and Theorem 3 on page 17 gives the one-step projection rate.
The paper derives a Hölder CATE minimax elbow using localized fuzzy hypotheses and a localized higher-order estimator.

Corollary 9.1 attains the scalar missing-response functional rate \(n^{-(2\alpha+2\beta)/(2\alpha+2\beta+d)}\) with projection-kernel higher-order estimating equations under its stated regularity conditions.
Theorem 4.1 derives the efficient influence function for a deconfounding flow-matching moment, and the subsequent one-step expansion establishes first-order efficiency under nuisance conditions.
The public abstract announces Hölder counterfactual-density minimax rates and localized fuzzy hypotheses but does not reveal the loss, exact class, formula, or theorem text.

In arXiv:2605.10206v1, Definition 1 and equations (1)--(2) define extended Wasserstein loss as the target-design average of statewise outcome-space \(W_1\); Theorem 2 gives a logarithmically inflated continuous-conditioning upper bound under an implementation-transfer condition, and Theorem 3 gives the lower bound, so the two sides are matched only up to logarithmic and transfer factors.

body.tldr: The known-uniform-design benchmark isolates a way marginal counterfactual generation can be harder than direct smooth-density estimation: the same rough propensity field is reused across all outcome locations even though the covariate distribution itself is known. The target is marginal-mixture \(W_1\), which is strictly weaker than GANICE's design-averaged statewise extended Wasserstein loss; an explicit smooth separation prevents importing that paper's lower bound or continuous-conditioning upper/lower theory, while convexity preserves a one-way, generally nonsharp upper-bound implication. The project asks for the complete minimax expected \(W_1\) frontier over this positive sectional-Hölder class, including critical logarithms and an if-and-only-if oracle boundary. Its proved negative side uses a shared-sign causal mixture whose marginal transport separation survives covariate averaging; its proposed positive side requires simultaneous finite-order correction of a growing outcome-wavelet dictionary followed by finite Kantorovich--Rubinstein projection. The representative legal tuple \(d=1,m=6,s=4,\alpha=\beta=27/200\) yields the proposed lower exponent \(243/697\), strictly slower than both scalar and oracle comparators. The full asymmetric known-design match, not that isolated bound or a claim about general factual generators, is the headline open content.

project_justification.gap: Even with the covariate law fixed and known to be uniform, DoubleGen's oracle transfer and first-order nuisance bound do not determine whether rough propensity and treated conditional-density sections enlarge marginal \(W_1\) risk. GANICE develops continuous-conditioning minimax upper/lower theory for design-averaged statewise Wasserstein loss, matched only up to logarithmic and implementation-transfer factors, but a smooth positive pair can have positive statewise-average distance and identical marginal mixtures, so its lower bound and continuous-conditioning upper/lower theory do not settle this target. Direct \(W_1\) density theory removes confounding, fixed counterfactual-density projections do not reconstruct a refining law, and the public ACIC 2023 announcement does not expose a theorem that settles this exact known-design multivariate loss.
project_justification.niche: The missing benchmark is a same-class all-estimator frontier that holds the covariate design fixed and known, thereby isolating how outcome dimension, outcome smoothness, and separate propensity and covariate-sectional smoothness interact through marginal-mixture transport rather than through covariate-density estimation or averaged conditional transport.
project_justification.fill: A shared-propensity multiscale lower construction proves a nuisance-sensitive same-class converse. The proposed route to a match is a high-rank higher-order coefficient estimator exploiting the known uniform basis geometry, followed by finite probability projection. Completing that route and matching every regime and critical logarithm would yield the known-design marginal-mixture frontier and necessary-and-sufficient oracle boundary; these remain `oeq:high-rank-coefficient-certificate` and `oeq:sharp-frontier`.

body.related_work: LuedtkeFukumizu2025DoubleGen is a procedure-side motivation anchor: its Introduction studies direct marginal counterfactual generation, Theorem 2 transfers oracle lower bounds, Theorem 3 gives a conditional total-variation upper bound with a first-order nuisance-product term, and Section 7 asks for a sharper lower bound when nuisances are nonsmooth. For any fixed DoubleGen loss, generator class, and nuisance-map classes for which its boundary and mixed-Lipschitz hypotheses are separately verified, its oracle-transfer and nuisance-product results apply to that specified procedure; this observation neither defines a subfamily of the present model nor asserts that the lower-bound alternatives satisfy those procedure-dependent hypotheses. TamanoImaizumi2026GANICE studies a different causal loss. In arXiv:2605.10206v1, Definition 1 and equations (1)--(2) define extended Wasserstein distance as the target-design average of statewise outcome-space \(W_1\). Theorem 2 gives a logarithmically inflated continuous-conditioning upper bound under an implementation-transfer condition, and Theorem 3 gives the lower bound, so the upper and lower theory is matched only up to logarithmic and transfer factors. The smooth construction in prop:ganice-loss-separation has identical marginal mixtures but positive statewise-average distance, so GANICE's lower bound and continuous-conditioning upper/lower theory do not transfer to this proposal's marginal-mixture \(W_1\); the convexity inequality in that proposition shows that compatible extended-loss upper bounds can still yield generally nonsharp marginal upper bounds. In the primary author version arXiv:1902.01778v4 of NilesWeedBerthet2022, Section 2.2.1, Theorem 1 and its displayed bound on PDF page 6 give the positive-density upper rate over the stated Besov class, while Theorem 3 and its displayed bound on the same page give the corresponding all-estimator lower rate. At transport order \(1\) and density dimension \(m\ge3\), their oracle exponent is \((s+1)/(2s+m)\); prop:oracle-randomized-reduction requires that exponent on the present classical Hölder submodel rather than treating the published Besov formulation as a conditional-density assumption. Section 3, Theorem 4 gives the negative-Besov comparison, and Section 4.1 constructs the wavelet estimate and projects it to a density. In the primary arXiv:2102.12034v1 source corresponding to KennedyBalakrishnanWasserman2023, equation (3) on PDF page 4 defines the same marginal counterfactual density, whereas equation (6) on page 6 fixes a finite-dimensional projection; Theorem 1 with equation (17) on page 13 gives its efficient influence function, and Theorem 3 on page 17 gives the one-step projection rate. These exact locators separate the refining law-valued \(W_1\) target here from their fixed-projection theory. RobinsEtAl2017HOIF supplies the projection-kernel U-statistic architecture and, under its additional projection and nuisance regularity conditions, Corollary 9.1's scalar missing-response rate. LiuEtAl2017EmpiricalHOIF motivates empirical kernels for an unknown covariate density but does not justify the present known-uniform-design assumption; here it informs only the correction architecture. KennedyEtAl2024MinimaxCATE supplies the localized fuzzy-hypothesis and localized higher-order elbow template, but its Hölder conditions concern scalar propensity, regression, and CATE functions rather than conditional-density sections, and its target is pointwise CATE rather than a transported marginal law. KimKimKennedy2018 gives first-order doubly robust density estimation under \(L_q\) loss, and LuedtkeChung2024 gives regularized Hilbert-valued one-step inference; neither addresses this known-design global \(W_1\) frontier. DanceEtAl2026DecFM derives an efficient influence correction for a flow-matching moment and motivates a benchmark consumer, but its broader unknown-design setting is not covered by this theorem. KaddourEtAl2025Survey catalogs causal generative modeling but does not state a nuisance-sensitive known-design marginal Wasserstein frontier. Kennedy2023ACIC is disclosed as priority-relevant but externally unverifiable beyond its public abstract; exact loss, model, rate, and possible subsumption remain a source-verification kill test, and no first counterfactual-density minimax claim is made.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The all-count shared-sign mixture calculation, continuous Hölder construction, fixed-sample testing reduction, and representative exponent arithmetic are proved in `thm:interaction-lower-envelope` and `prop:representative-nonoracle`. The central upper certificate is unproved when scale-dependent covariate rank exceeds sample size; a deterministic Neumann remainder does not control high-order degenerate variance. An upper wavelet sum can suggest a critical logarithm but cannot certify its necessity without a matching multiscale lower construction. The smooth GANICE loss separation is finite-dimensional and explicit, but it does not itself supply any marginal-mixture lower rate. The ACIC 2023 abstract remains a priority obligation because no accessible full theorem text was located.
body.honest_scope: The target is the marginal law of \(Y(1)\), not design-averaged statewise Wasserstein loss, an individual-effect law, or inference for a nonsmooth scalar Wasserstein functional. The covariate law is fixed and known to be uniform, so the theorem is a known-design benchmark and does not claim the frontier for general factual generators with an unknown covariate law. DoubleGen comparisons are procedure-side and require separate verification of its loss-, generator-, and nuisance-class hypotheses; no DoubleGen law subfamily is defined here. GANICE's extended-loss lower bound and continuous-conditioning minimax upper/lower theory do not transfer to marginal-mixture \(W_1\), although compatible upper bounds may transfer nonsharply by convexity. The ambient arm \(0\) conditional law is unrestricted and unlinked to arm \(1\); a uniform arm \(0\) appears only in the named lower-bound witness subfamily and the explicit loss-separation witness. Uniform conditional-density bounds and separate uniform sectional Hölder conditions are deliberate nonstandard primitives of the benchmark and are not attributed to the direct-density or scalar CATE comparators. The fixed tuple has asymptotic \(n\) scope and smoothness adaptation is excluded. The theorem concerns a compact positive-density treated-arm model and does not assert that raw CelebA pixels satisfy the Hölder restrictions. The scalar \(m=1\) HIV example motivates the distributional consumer but is outside the stated \(m\ge3\) theorem. The no-confounding submodel must reproduce the Niles-Weed--Berthet oracle rate exponent.
